los.text: Perform a competent upper limb neurological examination with increased confidence.
los.html:
• Full routine: see ICM Year 1 › Neurology & cognition › LO 1 (inspection, tone, power, reflexes, coordination, sensation).
"Increased confidence" checklist
Explain each step to the patient as you go ("push up against me")
Always compare left and right at each muscle group
  • Grade power on the MRC scale: 0 none
  • 1 flicker
  • 2 movement with gravity eliminated
  • 3 against gravity
  • 4 against some resistance
  • 5 normal
Use reinforcement before calling a reflex absent
Map sensory loss: dermatome (root), peripheral nerve (median, ulnar, radial) or glove (neuropathy)
Finish: "I'd also examine the lower limbs and cranial nerves"

los.text: Interpret basic clinical signs identified during a respiratory examination.
los.html:
FindingInterpretation
Tracheal deviation awayTension pneumothorax, large effusion
Tracheal deviation towardsCollapse, pneumonectomy, fibrosis
Reduced expansion on one sidePathology on that side
Dull percussion + bronchial breathing + increased vocal resonanceConsolidation (pneumonia)
Stony dull + reduced breath sounds and vocal resonancePleural effusion
Hyper-resonant + reduced breath soundsPneumothorax
Fine end-inspiratory cracklesPulmonary fibrosis, pulmonary oedema
Coarse cracklesBronchiectasis, infection
Wheeze (polyphonic, expiratory)Asthma, COPD
ClubbingLung cancer, fibrosis, bronchiectasis, empyema (not COPD alone)
CO₂ retention flap, bounding pulseType 2 respiratory failure

los.text: Perform a competent respiratory examination with increased confidence
los.html:
• Full routine: see ICM Year 1 › Respiratory › LO 2.
Focus for fluency
Hands → face → neck → chest front → chest back → finishing steps, without prompts
Expansion: hands round the chest, thumbs meeting in the midline; watch the thumbs move apart
Percussion: compare like with like, include the axillae and apices (clavicle)
Vocal resonance: "say 99", compare sides
Present findings that fit together into a diagnosis

los.text: Interpret basic clinical signs identified during a respiratory examination.
los.html:
• Same interpretation table as ICM Year 1 › Respiratory › LO 7
    • practise linking signs to one diagnosis: e.g. "dull percussion, bronchial breathing and coarse crackles at the right base suggest right lower lobe consolidation".

los.text: Insert a peripheral cannula into a model while adhering to aseptic non-touch technique (ANTT) guidelines.
los.html:
1Check indication, patient identity, explain, consent, allergies.
2
  • Hand hygiene
  • Prepare a clean tray (ANTT): cannula (pink 20G routine, green 18G or larger for fluids/blood, grey 16G in trauma)
  • Dressing
  • Flush (saline)
  • Extension set
  • Chlorhexidine/alcohol wipe
  • Sharps bin
  • Gloves
  • Tourniquet.
3Apply the tourniquet, choose a straight vein (back of hand or forearm; avoid joints, the side of a fistula, lymphoedema or a stroke-affected arm).
4Clean the site for 30 s and allow to dry; don't re-palpate.
5
  • Anchor the vein
  • Insert bevel up at 10–30°
  • Watch for flashback
  • Advance a few mm more
  • Then slide the cannula off the needle.
6Release the tourniquet, press over the vein tip, remove the needle, sharps straight into the bin.
7Attach the extension and flush with 5–10 mL saline (no swelling or pain), secure with a sterile dressing.
8Document (date, time, site, size, VIP score); review daily.

los.text: Identify common urological complaints and associated symptoms.
los.html:
ComplaintQuestions
Loin/flank painColicky, loin to groin (renal colic), fever (infection above a stone)
HaematuriaVisible or non-visible, painless (cancer) or painful (stone, infection), clots
Lower urinary tract symptomsStorage: frequency, urgency, nocturia, incontinence; voiding: hesitancy, poor stream, straining, terminal dribbling, incomplete emptying
DysuriaUTI, STI
RetentionCan't pass urine, painful (acute) or painless with overflow (chronic)
IncontinenceStress (cough, laugh) vs urge
ScrotalPain, swelling, lumps
BackgroundPrevious stones, prostate problems, catheters, medications (anticholinergics, diuretics), smoking (bladder cancer)

los.text: Begin to recognise red flags and urgent symptoms within the urological system.
los.html:
Red flagConcern
Painless visible haematuria (age ≥45)Bladder or kidney cancer: 2-week-wait referral
Fever with loin pain and an obstructing stoneObstructed infected kidney: emergency drainage
Sudden severe testicular pain (young male)Testicular torsion: emergency surgery within 6 hours
Acute urinary retentionCatheterise
Saddle anaesthesia, bladder/bowel dysfunction, bilateral sciaticaCauda equina syndrome
Anuria, rising creatinineBilateral obstruction, AKI
Weight loss, bone pain, raised PSAProstate cancer
Painless testicular lumpTesticular cancer
